site.title: Lymark — watermark with date, time and address on field photos
site.description: Android application that stamps time, date, day of the week, address and a tracking code on inspection and service proof photos.

hero.heading: The photo comes out of your phone already saying when, where and what.
hero.description: Lymark stamps the time, date, day of the week, address and a tracking code directly on the image. The file that comes out of the app already has the information embedded — it's not data that accompanies the photo and gets lost in the first WhatsApp forwarding.
hero.cta: Open the app in your browser

features.title: What goes into the image

time.heading: From the device clock, at the time of capture
time.description: A button returns the three fields to the current time when the capture took longer than expected. All remain editable.

address.heading: Filled by GPS, manually correctable
address.description: The street is abbreviated and the state becomes an acronym, so the address fits in two lines without covering the photo. If you typed before the GPS responded, what you wrote prevails.

code.heading: Fourteen characters, drawn by cryptographic generator
code.description: Used to cite a specific photo in a service order or report. It goes rotated on the right side or next to the data block, your choice.

features.note: Each field is turned on or off individually, and the block can be anchored in any of the four corners — in three sizes. The preview uses your current photo, not a generic example: what appears on the screen is literally what is exported.

process.title: The path of a photo

capture.heading: Camera or gallery
capture.description: The address starts being searched as soon as the photo comes in. The fields remain open for adjustment while this happens.

save.heading: Goes to the device gallery
save.description: It stays with the other photos on the phone, available for any application — even after uninstalling Lymark.

share.heading: Opens the system sheet
share.description: WhatsApp, email, Drive: the destination is chosen by the operating system, and the application does not participate in sending.

process.note: The two actions are separated on purpose. Saving and sharing solve different problems, and combining them into one button would force those who just want to archive to go through a sending screen.

data.title: Where your data is

device.heading: Photos, addresses and history
device.description: Lymark has no server, does not create an account and does not send your photos anywhere. The history saves the last two hundred exports in files from the application itself.

external.heading: Only coordinate-to-address conversion
external.description: To transform latitude and longitude into a readable address, the operating system consults Google's or Apple's geocoding service. This is the only information that goes out, and it goes through the system, not the application.

availability.description: Lymark is at version 1.3.0, in testing on Android before publication on the Google Play. There is no iOS version or web version, and the app does not collect payment.
